question: A patient with a suspected ectopic pregnancy complains of sudden, sharp pain in her right shoulder. Why does this happen?

options.A: Anxiety is causing muscle tension in her upper body.
options.B: Blood in her pelvis has irritated her diaphragm.
options.C: She strained her shoulder muscle while feeling dizzy.
options.D: An infection has spread upward to her lungs.

explanation: This is a classic nursing nugget! Blood pooling in the belly can irritate the phrenic nerve, which shares pathways with the shoulder. That's why pain shows up there! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h3)

question: What is the main danger if a third-degree tear is missed and left unrepaired after childbirth?

options.A: Delayed involution of the uterus and heavy lochia
options.B: Long-term fecal incontinence and painful intercourse
options.C: Chronic pelvic inflammatory disease and infertility
options.D: Permanent loss of bladder control and urine leakage

explanation: If sphincter damage isn't caught and repaired properly, it can lead to lifelong struggles with bowel control and painful sex. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h4)

question: What is the primary difference between an arranged marriage and a forced marriage?

options.A: The involvement of religious leaders
options.B: The age of the individuals getting married
options.C: The right to refuse and give full consent
options.D: The geographic location of the ceremony

explanation: In an arranged marriage, the individuals still have the freedom to say no, whereas a forced marriage happens without their consent. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h1)

question: What is a community health nurse's key role in preventing reservoir-based illnesses?

options.A: Isolating all livestock in urban residential neighborhoods
options.B: Designing and building modern municipal water treatment plants
options.C: Writing national health policies for pharmaceutical manufacturing
options.D: Educating the public on hygiene, waste disposal, and safe food storage

explanation: You are a teacher at heart! Teaching families simple hygiene and food safety habits is one of our most powerful prevention tools. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h7)

question: Besides sharing new rules, what must effective communication include during a healthcare transition?

options.A: An explanation of why the change improves patient outcomes
options.B: Strict orders that forbid nurses from asking questions
options.C: Detailed financial records of the hospital budget
options.D: Immediate disciplinary threats for non-compliant staff members

explanation: When nurses see the 'why'—especially how it helps patients—they are much more willing to get on board. [learn more](GST319_U2_T5#GST319_U2_T5_h5)

question: A patient asks why her body doesn't reject the developing pregnancy as a foreign object. What is the best way to explain this?

options.A: The baby carries the exact same blood type as the mother always
options.B: The placenta completely blocks all maternal blood cells from forming
options.C: The mother's immune system shuts down completely during pregnancy
options.D: The outer trophoblast layer actively modifies local immune responses

explanation: The placenta and outer cells are clever—they whisper to the immune system to stay calm so the baby can grow safely. Clinical communication made simple! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h5)

question: What are haematinics?

options.A: Enzymes that break down dietary proteins
options.B: Hormones that stimulate white cell immunity
options.C: Proteins that destroy old red blood cells
options.D: Nutrients needed for blood cell formation

explanation: Think of haematinics as the body's building blocks (like iron and vitamins) used to manufacture fresh, healthy red blood cells. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U1_T6#GNS223_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which parts of a sterile surgical gown are considered safe to touch as a sterile team member?

options.A: The neckline and the inner ties used to secure the back closure
options.B: The chest area down to the table level and the sleeves from above the elbow to the cuffs
options.C: The entire back of the gown from the shoulders all the way down to the hemline
options.D: The lower skirt of the gown below the level of the sterile instrument table

explanation: Remember: only the front from chest to table level and the sleeves are sterile. The back of the gown is always considered unsterile! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h4)

question: What happens inside the eye of a person with cataracts?

options.A: The natural lens becomes cloudy and blocks clear light
options.B: The macula breaks down and destroys central vision
options.C: Intraocular pressure rises and damages the optic nerve
options.D: Tiny blood vessels on the retina burst and bleed

explanation: Cataracts are characterized by the opacification or clouding of the eye's natural lens, which blurs the incoming light. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h2)

question: A patient says, 'I cannot be healthy because I am too weak to go to work and look after my children.' Which health model are they using?

options.A: Clinical model
options.B: Role performance model
options.C: Eudaimonistic model
options.D: Biological germ model

explanation: Spot on! This model measures health by whether a person can successfully carry out their daily family and job responsibilities. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why are local drama and folk media effective strategies in community mobilisation?

options.A: They provide a strict legal punishment for people who ignore health advice
options.B: They communicate health messages using culturally familiar and engaging entertainment
options.C: They force the government to release emergency healthcare funds instantly
options.D: They replace the need for any professional medical staff in the clinic

explanation: Drama and songs capture attention and break down complex health ideas into relatable stories. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why do doctors often use laparoscopy to look closely at the fallopian tubes?

options.A: It requires no anesthesia and is done at the bedside
options.B: It completely cures all tubal blockages
options.C: It uses high-frequency sound waves to measure organ density
options.D: It lets the surgeon see the pelvic organs directly with a camera

explanation: A laparoscope is a tiny lighted camera that gives the surgeon a clear, direct view of what is going on inside the pelvis. You're mastering this topic! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h4)

question: What do we call a dangerously low level of oxygen in the blood?

options.A: Hemothorax
options.B: Atelectasis
options.C: Hypoxemia
options.D: Hypercapnia

explanation: Well done! 'Hypo-' means low, and 'oxemia' refers to oxygen in the blood. Put them together and you have hypoxemia. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T12#GNS213_U2_T12_h2)

question: What is a major risk to watch out for when someone takes testosterone replacement therapy?

options.A: Sudden permanent hair loss
options.B: Excessive red blood cell production
options.C: Rapid increase in bone density
options.D: Severe drop in blood pressure

explanation: Testosterone gives a nudge to the bone marrow to make more red blood cells, which can sometimes push the count too high (polycythemia). [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why is agoraphobia often closely tied to panic attacks?

options.A: Agoraphobia only occurs immediately after a heart attack
options.B: Panic attacks always cure agoraphobia over time
options.C: Patients with agoraphobia never feel anxious in crowds
options.D: Patients fear they cannot escape easily if panic strikes

explanation: Agoraphobia is all about dreading public spaces where escaping or getting help during a sudden panic wave would feel impossible. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T6#GNS314_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is zero-based budgeting?

options.A: Cutting all nursing salaries down to zero during a financial crisis
options.B: Simply adding five percent to whatever was spent last year
options.C: Requiring departments to justify all expenses from scratch every year
options.D: Operating the hospital with zero money until donations arrive

explanation: Zero-based budgeting forces managers to prove the value of every single cost rather than just copying the previous year. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h4)

question: In maritime healthcare, what does the abbreviation TMAS stand for?

options.A: Transport Medical Action System
options.B: Trauma Management At Sea
options.C: Total Maritime Air Support
options.D: Telemedical Assistance Service

explanation: You got it! TMAS connects ships at sea with land-based medical experts for remote guidance and advice. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h5)

question: What happens to most primary oocytes before a girl even reaches puberty?

options.A: They rapidly divide into multiple active ova
options.B: They die off through a process called atresia
options.C: They immediately finish their second meiotic division
options.D: They migrate out of the ovaries into the fallopian tubes

explanation: Don't worry if this sounds harsh—it's a natural body process called atresia. Many eggs naturally degenerate over time even before puberty. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h2)

question: What are the three core components of the epidemiological triad?

options.A: Symptoms, diagnosis, and recovery
options.B: Agent, host, and environment
options.C: Prevention, treatment, and cure
options.D: Patient, nurse, and doctor

explanation: The epidemiological triad relies on the interaction between the infectious agent, the susceptible host, and the surrounding environment. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T17#GNS313_U1_T17_h2)

question: You visit a diabetic patient and notice their insulin is stored next to open food in a messy kitchen. What should you do?

options.A: Report the family to the local police department for negligence
options.B: Immediately discharge the patient from the home care program
options.C: Educate the patient and family on safe medication storage and hygiene
options.D: Leave the medication where it is since it is their private home

explanation: As a nurse, you are a teacher! Patient and family education fixes safety risks gently while respecting their living situation. Well done. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T7#GNS324_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of dietary counselling?

options.A: Diagnosing rare metabolic disorders through physical examination
options.B: Handing out strict, identical meal plans to every hospital patient
options.C: Prescribing high-cost nutritional supplements for rapid weight loss
options.D: Helping clients make sustainable food choices for better health

explanation: Dietary counselling focuses on guiding clients toward lasting, healthy eating habits tailored to their specific lives, rather than just giving out rigid paperwork. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h1)

question: A father is admitted for chronic hypertension. Why should the nurse involve his spouse and children in his discharge education?

options.A: Family members must take over the patient's job responsibilities
options.B: Hospital regulations require at least three visitors per patient
options.C: It prevents the patient from speaking to the doctor alone
options.D: The family functions as a unit, and lifestyle changes require household support

explanation: Diet and lifestyle changes are much easier to maintain when the whole family understands and participates in them. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h2)

question: In a research framework, what is the dependent variable?

options.A: The presumed cause of the health problem
options.B: The outcome or effect being measured
options.C: The abstract mental image with no label
options.D: The personal opinion of the lead nurse

explanation: Remember: the dependent variable is your final result or outcome. It's what changes in response to whatever you are testing! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h4)

question: What does 'informed consent' require before you start any clinical procedure on a patient?

options.A: Verbal approval given only by the hospital director
options.B: Signing a document without reading the risks
options.C: Voluntary permission after understanding risks and benefits
options.D: Payment of all hospital bills in advance

explanation: Informed consent is all about respect! The patient must fully understand the treatment, risks, and options, and then freely agree to go ahead. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h7)

question: When caring for someone at the end of life, who do we consider as the true unit of care?

options.A: The hospital ward staff
options.B: The dying patient alone
options.C: The entire family unit
options.D: The attending physician

explanation: In nursing, end-of-life care is never just about the patient alone. We look after the whole family because they share the emotional and psychological journey too! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T8#GNS221_U4_T8_h1)

question: What is the main goal of filling out that monthly injection safety monitoring form?

options.A: To schedule annual leave periods for the clinical team
options.B: To evaluate the bedside nursing skills of newly hired staff
options.C: To guarantee an uninterrupted supply of safety devices
options.D: To determine the salary scales for hospital administrators

explanation: You got it! The form helps us keep an eye on stock levels so our clinic never suddenly runs out of syringes and safety boxes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h2)

question: What is a major practical challenge when trying to prosecute FGM offenders in local Nigerian courts?

options.A: Mandatory legalization of the practice by state governors
options.B: Complete absence of any federal or state legal frameworks
options.C: Immunity granted to all traditional practitioners by the constitution
options.D: Lack of training and logistical support for police and judiciary

explanation: Correct! Law enforcement officers sometimes struggle to investigate and take these cases to court due to limited resources and specialized training. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T5#GNS225_U6_T5_h4)

question: Which heart chamber is responsible for pumping freshly oxygenated blood out to the rest of the newborn's body?

options.A: Right atrium
options.B: Left ventricle
options.C: Left atrium
options.D: Right ventricle

explanation: The left ventricle receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and pumps it into the aorta to supply the systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h6)

question: In infection control, what do we call a non-living object like a stethoscope or door handle that can pass germs from one person to another?

options.A: An insect carrying a disease
options.B: A contaminated inanimate object
options.C: The natural home of a pathogen
options.D: A break in the human skin

explanation: Spot on! In nursing, we call these non-living items 'fomites'. They easily pick up germs in the ward and carry them to the next patient if we don't clean our hands or equipment. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which type of ovarian cyst can contain unusual tissues like hair or teeth?

options.A: Follicular cyst
options.B: Dermoid cyst
options.C: Endometrioma
options.D: Corpus luteum cyst

explanation: Dermoid cysts sound a bit wild, but they just develop from germ cells and can sometimes contain quirky tissues like skin, hair, or teeth! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T32#GNS216_U5_T32_h2)

question: A nurse, a pharmacist, and a ward manager need to discuss a complex treatment plan for a critical patient. Which meeting format should they use?

options.A: Hospital board meeting
options.B: Administrative budget briefing
options.C: Multidisciplinary case conference
options.D: General staff handover

explanation: When different health professionals team up for a tricky patient case, it's called a multidisciplinary case conference. [learn more](GST321_U7_T4#GST321_U7_T4_h2)

question: What does a family's ability to buy food mainly depend on?

options.A: Local government policies on soil fertilization.
options.B: Total income, employment stability, and market food prices.
options.C: Global weather patterns and international shipping laws.
options.D: The distance from the nearest agricultural research center.

explanation: Exactly! Purchasing power simply means how much money is coming into the house compared to how much food actually costs in the market. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h2)

question: What is the best way to handle a young child who refuses to eat a newly introduced vegetable?

options.A: Offer it repeatedly over time alongside familiar foods without forcing them
options.B: Punish the child by sending them away from the dinner table immediately
options.C: Stop offering all vegetables permanently to avoid any further stress
options.D: Force the child to finish every single bite on the plate before sleeping

explanation: Children often need multiple exposures to a new food before accepting it, and pressure only increases mealtime anxiety. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h6)

question: Which psychological effect is commonly experienced by individuals undergoing quarantine?

options.A: Anxiety and boredom
options.B: Complete emotional euphoria
options.C: Permanent memory loss
options.D: Increased desire for heavy labor

explanation: Restriction of movement and uncertainty often lead to stress, anxiety, and boredom among confined individuals. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h7)

question: What usually pushes someone to start a very strict food fad?

options.A: An innate biological need to consume fewer than five hundred calories
options.B: A clinical requirement to study human metabolism in real-time
options.C: A professional obligation to test new commercial food products
options.D: A desire for control and quick solutions to personal anxieties

explanation: When life feels overwhelming, people often use strict food rules to regain a sense of personal control. You're doing amazing! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h2)

question: Why must you check if two drugs are compatible before adding an IV piggyback medicine into an existing line?

options.A: Hospital pharmacy software blocks incompatible infusions anyway.
options.B: Primary fluids neutralize the therapeutic effect of all antibiotics.
options.C: Incompatible drugs can form precipitates that block the catheter.
options.D: Mismatched drugs will automatically cause severe patient hypertension.

explanation: Spot on! Mixing the wrong drugs can cause chemical reactions that turn into solid gunk, clogging the line and endangering the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T15#GNS122_U1_T15_h6)

question: How do interferons protect your body from viral infections?

options.A: They wrap around viruses and digest them.
options.B: They raise body temperature to burn up viral particles.
options.C: They warn nearby healthy cells to put up their defenses against viruses.
options.D: They tell the bone marrow to make extra red blood cells.

explanation: Think of interferons as chemical text messages sent by infected cells to warn their healthy neighbors: 'A virus is coming, lock your doors!' [learn more](GST114_U4_T4#GST114_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the main difference between 'perfect use' and 'typical use' of a contraceptive method?

options.A: Typical use accounts for human error and real-life inconsistencies
options.B: Typical use always has a higher success rate than perfect use
options.C: Perfect use is calculated only in elderly clients
options.D: Perfect use includes the cost of purchasing the supply items

explanation: Perfect use assumes the method is used flawlessly every single time, while typical use reflects real human life—like missing a pill or a barrier breaking. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T5#GNS225_U3_T5_h5)

question: Why is it important to run physical medical tests on someone presenting with severe anxiety symptoms?

options.A: To determine the correct dosage of psychotherapy immediately
options.B: To measure the exact concentration of brain neurotransmitters
options.C: To rule out medical conditions like hyperthyroidism that mimic anxiety
options.D: To prove that the patient is faking psychological distress

explanation: Spot on! Conditions like an overactive thyroid can cause a racing pulse and tremors that look just like anxiety. We always check the physical body first! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T1#GNS324_U4_T1_h4)

question: What should a home health nurse do when preparing to change a sterile wound dressing in a cluttered living room?

options.A: Ask the family to leave the house for the entire day
options.B: Improvise a clean working field and use a portable sharps container
options.C: Skip sterile technique because the home environment is not a hospital
options.D: Perform the procedure on the floor to avoid touching dirty tables

explanation: Nurses must adapt to home environments by creating clean surfaces for supplies and safely discarding needles in portable containers. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which task is part of the relief distribution duties of disaster agencies?

options.A: Delivering food and temporary shelter to displaced persons
options.B: Writing new national laws for civil aviation safety
options.C: Setting interest rates for commercial business loans
options.D: Conducting routine dental checks in public schools

explanation: Relief distribution is all about meeting basic human survival needs—like food, clean water, and shelter—for people forced out of their homes. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h4)

question: If a patient shows clear signs of shock after eating an allergen, which classic symptom might actually be completely missing?

options.A: Severe stomach cramps
options.B: Swelling of the tongue
options.C: Hives or skin rashes
options.D: Difficulty breathing

explanation: Surprise! Up to 20% of severe anaphylaxis cases don't show any skin rashes or hives. Never rule out anaphylaxis just because the skin looks clear. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h4)

question: Why does maternal hyperglycemia lead to macrosomia in the developing fetus?

options.A: Excess amniotic fluid stretches the fetal bones
options.B: Maternal fat deposits transfer directly to the baby
options.C: High fetal insulin acts as a growth promoter
options.D: The placenta grows larger to absorb extra water

explanation: Excess glucose from the mother triggers the baby to make too much insulin, and insulin acts like a growth hormone that causes the baby to grow unusually large. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h3)

question: What is the main goal of public health policies in government?

options.A: To stop foreign doctors from visiting
options.B: To close down all primary healthcare centers
options.C: To guide resource distribution and structure healthcare delivery
options.D: To make huge profits for drug manufacturing companies

explanation: Correct! Policies act like a roadmap. They give government agencies the rules and structure they need to organize, fund, and deliver healthcare properly. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T26#GNS225_U5_T26_h2)

question: Which of these is a classic example of 'formal social control'?

options.A: Family members showing disappointment in a child
options.B: Neighbors gossiping about someone being rude
options.C: Police arrests and court fines for breaking laws
options.D: Community elders advising youth to behave well

explanation: That's right! Formal control uses official systems like laws, the police, and courts to keep order. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T4#GNS225_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why does a reentry circuit cause an arrhythmia?

options.A: It forces the heart muscle cells to permanently stop receiving oxygen
options.B: It traps an electrical signal in a looping pathway that causes rapid contractions
options.C: It immediately destroys the natural pacemaker cells in the right atrium
options.D: It completely blocks all electrical impulses from leaving the sinoatrial node

explanation: A reentry circuit occurs when an electrical wave gets stuck traveling in a circle, constantly re-stimulating the heart tissue to beat too fast. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h1)

question: What is the key sign that an abortion procedure is unsafe?

options.A: Done using standard medical pills prescribed by a doctor
options.B: Conducted inside a registered tertiary hospital facility
options.C: Performed strictly within the first four weeks of gestation
options.D: Performed by untrained persons or in unhygienic environments

explanation: Correct! Unsafe procedures usually happen in dirty places or are done by people without proper medical training. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h2)

question: What makes an abortion procedure classified as "unsafe"?

options.A: An elective termination performed using modern pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.C: A legal surgical procedure performed by a certified gynecologist
options.D: A termination done without proper medical training or in unsterile settings

explanation: You've got this! An unsafe abortion simply means it was carried out by untrained hands or in dirty places, which puts the patient at a huge risk for severe complications. Spotting this definition helps you protect your patients early! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h1)

question: Who are the best people to involve when mobilizing a local community for safer maternal health?

options.A: Factory owners and corporate bosses
options.B: Traditional rulers, religious leaders, and local community groups
options.C: Construction contractors and road engineers
options.D: International sports bodies and foreign embassies

explanation: Exactly! Local leaders have a huge influence on community health choices and are key partners in encouraging hospital deliveries. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h8)

question: A community nurse notices that an elderly client's primary caregiver looks extremely exhausted and frustrated. What is the best way to document this observation?

options.A: Record specific behavioral signs of fatigue in the caregiver and note the risk of burnout
options.B: Write that the family member is lazy and refuses to help the sick client
options.C: Document that the home environment is completely peaceful and supportive
options.D: Ignore the observation because the family member is not the official client

explanation: Documenting caregiver strain objectively helps the healthcare team plan interventions to support the family and protect the client. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following is a classic condition commonly managed using primary health care standing orders?

options.A: Neurosurgical trauma
options.B: Uncomplicated malaria
options.C: Open-heart surgery
options.D: Advanced chemotherapy

explanation: Uncomplicated malaria is a high-volume, routine primary care condition managed safely using standard diagnostic and treatment protocols. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is usually one of the very first signs when a patient starts developing serum sickness?

options.A: Severe chest pain
options.B: Yellowing of the eyes
options.C: An itchy skin rash
options.D: Sudden hair loss

explanation: An itchy, hive-like rash is often the body's early warning signal that serum sickness is starting. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h4)

question: Which piece of information is most critical to document immediately during a patient's admission assessment?

options.A: Known drug allergies
options.B: Favorite television programs
options.C: Previous occupation history
options.D: Preferred clothing brand

explanation: Documenting allergies immediately prevents the accidental administration of medications that could cause severe or life-threatening reactions. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which nursing action best describes a promotive reproductive health service?

options.A: Suturing a perineal tear following a normal vaginal delivery
options.B: Performing a manual vacuum aspiration for an incomplete miscarriage
options.C: Leading a community health talk on proper menstrual hygiene
options.D: Prescribing antibiotics for a confirmed pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Promotive services involve general health education and encouraging positive wellness practices rather than treating active disease. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical problem caused by poorly planned, excessive protein intake?

options.A: Potential for chronic constipation due to low fiber
options.B: Extra workload for the kidneys
options.C: Immediate development of type 1 diabetes
options.D: Increased risk of dehydration

explanation: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune condition where the body attacks its own insulin-making cells—it isn't caused by eating too much steak or beans! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h7)

question: What is a common local myth in Nigeria regarding modern contraceptives and young women?

options.A: That using them before having children causes permanent infertility
options.B: That they cause women to grow facial hair overnight
options.C: That they are only manufactured for elderly grandmothers
options.D: That they instantly cure all infectious diseases

explanation: This is a very common community worry. As future nurses, you'll help clear up this misconception by explaining that modern methods do not cause permanent damage. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h6)

question: In the FAST stroke assessment tool, what does the letter 'T' stand for?

options.A: Temperature of the patient's skin
options.B: Tremors in the fingers and hands
options.C: Total paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: Time to call emergency services

explanation: Time is brain! The 'T' reminds us to call for emergency help immediately when stroke signs appear, because quick action saves brain tissue. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T24#GNS222_U3_T24_h3)

question: How do you properly check the function of cranial nerve XI (the spinal accessory nerve) in an adult?

options.A: By checking if the patient can stick out their tongue straight
options.B: By shining a bright light into both of the patient's eyes
options.C: By asking the patient to shrug their shoulders against resistance
options.D: By testing the patient's ability to hear a whispered voice

explanation: Just place your hands on their shoulders and ask them to shrug against your push. That tests cranial nerve XI easily! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T4#GNS222_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why must a nurse take a detailed medical history before a client starts hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: To find out how many children the client's extended family prefers
options.B: To determine the exact date of the client's future menopause
options.C: To check for underlying conditions that might make certain hormones unsafe
options.D: To calculate the precise financial cost of the clinic visit

explanation: You're right! Conditions like a history of blood clots can make certain hormones unsafe, so checking health history first keeps the client safe. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h4)

question: Why should ear drops (otic drops) always be warmed to room temperature before putting them in?

options.A: Warming increases the antibiotic power
options.B: Cold drops can instantly burst the eardrum
options.C: Cold medication is too thick to pass through the ear canal
options.D: Cold drops can shock the inner ear and cause severe dizziness

question: Where does the greatest amount of water and nutrient reabsorption happen in the nephron?

question: What are the three core components of the epidemiological triangle used in public health?

options.C: Bacteria, virus, and fungus
options.D: Reservoir, vector, and portal

question: Which of these is NOT a role for a nurse doing community cancer advocacy?

question: Four hours after a normal vaginal delivery, a mum hasn't peed yet, and her uterus feels soft (boggy) and pushed to the right. What is likely happening?

question: Which cells make up the large majority of the outer layer of your skin (the epidermis)?

options.A: Melanocytes
options.B: Fibroblasts
options.C: Adipocytes

question: Why is it important to include health topics in the regular school timetable?

options.A: It replaces the need for any physical school infrastructure

options.C: It guarantees that every student will pursue a career in nursing
options.D: It equips them with lifelong knowledge to prevent illness and make good choices

explanation: Correct! Classroom lessons build health awareness, helping students practice healthy habits long after they leave school. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h5)

question: As a nurse, what is the best first step before handing out a sleeping pill?

options.A: Checking the patient's visual acuity in bright sunlight

options.C: Requiring the patient to sign a legal release form

question: Why is looking into a patient's eye with an ophthalmoscope so useful for checking whole-body health?

options.A: The eye mirrors the brain with 100% perfection
options.B: It lets doctors look directly at living tiny blood vessels and nerves
options.C: It is the only organ affected by high blood sugar

question: In secretory diarrhoea, why do patients lose water so quickly?

options.C: Stomach acid production increases to dangerous levels
options.D: The kidneys stop filtering waste products completely

question: Why do many patients like to use complementary therapies along with their regular care?

options.A: Because they are always cheaper than conventional drugs
options.B: To replace all standard prescription medications permanently
options.C: To align with personal wellness values and address chronic issues
options.D: Because orthodox doctors mandate them in all hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Patients often look for a whole-person approach that fits their personal beliefs, especially when dealing with long-term health challenges. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h1)

question: How does the hippocampus work when it comes to human memory?

options.A: It acts as the final permanent storage vault for every memory
options.B: It translates what you see into spoken words
options.C: It organizes new memories and helps send them to the cortex
options.D: It deletes sad memories to protect your mental health

explanation: Correct! Think of the hippocampus as a sorting station that processes new memories and helps ship them to the cerebral cortex for permanent storage. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h4)

question: Why is final reporting to the community an essential final step?

options.A: To prove to the government that the nurses deserve a salary raise
options.B: To fulfill a legal requirement so nurses can travel abroad
options.C: To advertise private clinics opening in nearby towns

question: How many bowel movements per week is typically used to help define constipation in pregnancy?

question: What is the medical term for the natural weakening of the immune system that happens as people get older?

options.A: Immunosenescence

options.C: Autoimmunity
options.D: Seroconversion

explanation: Well done! 'Immuno' relates to the immune system, and 'senescence' means growing older. Put them together and you get the age-related decline in immunity. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T4#GNS313_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why is dragging a patient straight across bedsheets a bad idea for their skin?

options.C: It creates friction and shear forces that damage skin and blood vessels

question: On an ECG tracing, what does the QRS complex stand for?

options.A: Sinoatrial node firing

options.C: Ventricular depolarization
options.D: Ventricular filling phase

explanation: The big QRS spike shows electricity rushing through the big lower chambers (ventricles) so they can pump blood out! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T16#GNS213_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is the primary function of the puborectalis muscle in bowel control?

options.A: Pumps blood away from the hemorrhoidal veins
options.B: Produces mucus to lubricate the anal canal
options.C: Senses the chemical composition of the stool
options.D: Creates an angle that helps keep stool in the rectum

question: What does it mean when we say quality improvement tests are 'iterative'?

options.A: They must be performed identically by every hospital in the country
options.B: They are repeated once every ten years by hospital executives
options.C: They involve running multiple small cycles that build upon each other
options.D: They are discarded immediately if the first attempt is imperfect

explanation: Think of 'iterative' as learning as you go. You run a small test, learn from it, and use that lesson to run the next, slightly better cycle! [learn more](GST319_U3_T4#GST319_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why should community health nurses know about laws protecting women and children?

options.A: So nurses can personally prosecute abusive husbands in a court of law

options.C: So they can rewrite traditional community inheritance customs themselves
options.D: So they can arrest community leaders who enforce patriarchal rules

explanation: While we aren't lawyers, knowing the law helps us connect distressed patients to the right agencies that can offer legal and social support. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T8#GNS225_U6_T8_h6)

question: A heart failure patient uses a wearable at home. Which trend should make a nurse step in early?

options.A: Gradual upward trends in daily weight and decreasing physical activity

options.C: Occasional reminders to stand up and stretch during sedentary hours

question: High rates of under-five mortality in a community usually point to problems with which of the following?

options.A: Preventable infections and nutrition

options.D: Excessive spending on surgical equipment

question: A patient takes the wrong BP meds and feels dizzy. What is your very first nursing action?

options.B: Assess vital signs and notify the attending physician right away
options.C: Wait for the patient to sleep off the medication effects

question: Why does a patch of skin get red and swollen when it becomes inflamed?

options.C: Skin cells multiply rapidly to form a shield

question: Why does severe facial and body swelling occur in nephrotic syndrome?

question: What is the most immediate life-threatening complication that can occur during the third stage of labor?

question: What do macroeconomic indicators provide for a country?

question: A confused elderly patient keeps holding pills in their cheek without swallowing them. What is this behavior called?

question: What is a common myth about nursing work in subacute facilities?

question: Which of these is a major barrier to using research in many Nigerian hospitals?

question: How do digital (electronic) blood pressure machines mainly measure your blood pressure?

question: On a standard WHO growth chart, what does the bottom (horizontal) line represent?

question: What is a major community-wide effect when a clinic suffers an outbreak of healthcare-associated infections?

question: What usually happens when the delicate hormonal balance of the female reproductive system is disrupted?

question: What does setting up a 'digital curfew' mean for healthy screen habits?

question: Why do resistant infections usually lead to much higher healthcare costs?

question: Why do pregnant mothers need extra amounts of nutrients like iron?

question: You just finished giving an IM injection on the ward. What is the safest thing to do right away?

question: Who do state-level anti-FGM laws mostly target for arrest?

question: Why is daily weight tracking so important for a patient taking oral prednisone?

question: Which of these is NOT a challenge facing Youth Friendly Services in Nigeria?

question: What is the main purpose of a pressure-mapping surface on a smart bed?

question: What details should you write down in the chart after doing passive range of motion exercises?

question: Which of these is a key advocacy role for a nurse working in a geriatric home?

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when validating your clinic's data?

question: Why do health programs brought in from the outside often fail if the locals aren't involved?

question: What is the primary substance used as a contrast medium during a barium swallow procedure?

question: Why are bedside nurses considered the frontline defenders in clinical risk management?

question: What is a key focus when nursing an expectant mother who has chronic kidney disease?

question: Which situation is an example of cross-contamination from poor glove habits?

question: Which common oral side effect should you warn patients about if they are taking phenytoin long-term?

question: Why might a patient on a ventilator for a long time be switched from an ordinary breathing tube (endotracheal tube) to a tracheostomy?

question: What does cervical mucus look and feel like when it is most favorable for sperm survival around ovulation?

question: Which lab finding is a well-known kidney side effect of long-term D-penicillamine use?

question: Why is it recommended to gently press on the tragus after instilling ear drops?

question: How does losing access to school affect a young bride's future?

question: A patient with completely clear breathing sounds inhaled a toxic gas two hours ago. What should you, as the nurse, expect to do?

question: Why does a lack of health awareness stop patients from insisting on safe injections?

question: Why is the middle part (midpiece) of a sperm packed with mitochondria?

question: Which antibody class is the main driver behind severe allergic reactions like anaphylaxis?

question: How do fat-soluble (lipid-soluble) toxins act differently in the body compared to water-soluble ones?

question: A nurse is teaching range-of-motion exercises to a patient recovering from a stroke. Which level of prevention is this?

question: What actually happens during the 'promotion' stage of cancer development?

question: A patient with diabetes looks shaky, dizzy, and is sweating before lunch. What should the nurse do right away?

question: What exactly is an occupational health hazard?

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent medication errors?

question: Why is psychological support also offered to the family members of a recovering patient?

question: Why do special children typically require care that goes beyond routine pediatric visits?

question: In respiratory care, what does the term 'weaning' mean?

question: How do you properly test Cranial Nerve VII (the Facial nerve)?

question: Why must a gravity drainage bag always be positioned below the level of the wound?

question: A patient comes in with a warm, swollen, and painful knee after light activity. What is most likely going on?

question: What is the main goal of Primary Health Care (PHC) in a community?

question: What is the primary focus of microbiology in nursing practice?

question: Which heart chamber pumps oxygen-rich blood out into the main body artery (the aorta)?

question: Why are foods like whole grapes and hot dogs so dangerous for toddlers?

question: Severe dehydration in a pregnant patient can trigger which scary complication?

question: What simple home care helps most with scrotal swelling on the first day after surgery?

question: Which hospital objects are considered high-touch surfaces that need frequent cleaning?

question: What is the main reason lab scientists perform a crossmatch before releasing blood?

question: Why are secondary complications so dangerous for patients with brain or nerve injuries?

question: How is active surveillance different from passive surveillance?

explanation: Sometimes an antidote wears off before the poison is fully cleared from the body. Continuous monitoring ensures the patient doesn't suddenly slip back into toxicity. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T7#GNS215_U5_T7_h6)

question: A patient struggles with English, and her young son offers to translate for you. What is the best thing to do?

options.A: Use hand gestures instead of words to avoid needing any translation.
options.B: Accept the son's help immediately to save time on the ward.
options.C: Ask another nurse who is busy with medication to translate.
options.D: Request a certified medical interpreter to ensure accurate translation.

explanation: Correct! Certified interpreters keep things confidential and medically accurate, whereas family members might leave out important details. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the main use of an oxygen tent in children's wards?

options.A: Administering aerosolized chemotherapy drugs
options.B: Providing mechanical ventilation for adult trauma
options.C: Delivering controlled oxygen in pediatric care
options.D: Treating severe burn wounds in sterile isolation

explanation: Oxygen tents are super helpful in pediatric wards! They let us give steady oxygen to toddlers and young kids who might keep pulling off a standard face mask. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T10#GNS212_U2_T10_h1)

question: What is the correct sequence when putting on personal protective equipment before entering an isolation room?

options.A: Eye protection, gloves, gown, mask
options.B: Gloves, gown, mask, eye protection
options.C: Gown, mask, eye protection, gloves
options.D: Mask, gloves, gown, eye protection

explanation: Putting the gown on first and gloves last ensures the glove cuffs overlap the gown sleeves, leaving no exposed skin at the wrist. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h6)

question: When a patient suddenly stands up and feels dizzy from a drop in blood pressure, how does the body normally respond?

options.A: Increases parasympathetic output to slow the heart right down
options.B: Triggers sympathetic vasoconstriction and increases heart rate
options.C: Shuts down vasomotor tone to pool blood in the lower limbs
options.D: Signals the respiratory centre to stop breathing temporarily

explanation: To stop you from fainting, your cardiovascular centre quickly tightens up your blood vessels and speeds up your heart to push blood back up to your brain! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T14#GNS211_U3_T14_h3)

question: Before how many weeks of pregnancy do we consider labour to be preterm?

options.A: 40 weeks
options.B: 42 weeks
options.C: 37 weeks
options.D: 38 weeks

question: Why should children with viral infections like chickenpox or flu never be given aspirin?

options.A: It causes severe green discoloration of the teeth
options.B: It completely stops the heart from beating
options.C: It is linked to Reye's syndrome, a dangerous brain and liver condition
options.D: It has no effect on pediatric fevers

explanation: Aspirin during viral illnesses can trigger Reye's syndrome—a rare but severe condition affecting the brain and liver. Always choose paracetamol instead! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T6#GNS215_U6_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary function of carbohydrates in the human body?

options.A: Providing primary energy for daily activities
options.B: Producing essential hormones for growth
options.C: Regulating body temperature through sweating
options.D: Repairing damaged muscle tissues and organs

explanation: Carbohydrates are broken down into glucose, which serves as the body's main and most efficient energy source. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h1)

question: Which of these is considered a redundancy error in research writing?

options.C: Using the same font style for all headings in the paper
options.D: Placing explanatory footnotes below the table body

explanation: Listing every single table number word-for-word in your text is repetitive. Your text should just highlight the main trends instead! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h6)

question: Why must life-saving drugs like oxytocin be kept in a cold chain (refrigerated)?

options.A: Cold temperatures make the liquid solution taste much sweeter
options.B: Refrigeration prevents the glass ampoules from shattering
options.C: Freezing stops the plastic syringes from melting in storage
options.D: Heat exposure destroys the active potency of the medication

explanation: Exactly right! Uterotonics like oxytocin hate the heat; leaving them out in warm temperatures ruins their strength and effectiveness. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T11#GNS225_U3_T11_h7)

question: In community health, why can't just one type of health worker solve every problem?

options.A: Government policies forbid single-worker clinics
options.B: Doctors lack the training to visit local neighborhoods
options.C: Nurses refuse to handle community cases on their own
options.D: Community issues involve physical, social, and economic factors

question: What does a low p-value (less than 0.05) usually let a researcher do?

options.A: Reject the null hypothesis
options.B: Change the independent variable
options.C: Eliminate all confounding factors
options.D: Ignore ethical review boards

explanation: A low p-value means your findings are statistically significant and unlikely to just be a stroke of luck! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T10#GNS217_U3_T10_h7)

question: Why is catching a high-risk pregnancy early so important for us as nurses?

options.A: It guarantees that the baby will be born without any congenital defects

options.C: It allows the healthcare team to plan timely interventions and prevent complications
options.D: It removes the need for any laboratory tests during the third trimester

question: Which Nigerian agency handles drug law enforcement, arresting traffickers, and seizing illegal substances?
